# Independent audit: local radial simplex descent in all continuous dimensions

Source: `candidate 4e12bc9cd7731df3`.
Complete proof audited PASS, with no repair required. The source verifier
`supporting computation verify_all_dimensional_radial_simplex_descent_two_sided.py` was read and
run: the expanded version passes 2,829 exact checks. It independently constructs actual cut-edge
vertices and determinant volumes, not merely the claimed scalar formula.

## 1. Actual geometry and the inherited compact reduction

All projection, complete-base, positive-radius, rank-deficiency, finite-tilt,
vertical-cap, and uniform symmetric-difference arguments from the preceding
arbitrary-rank note are dimension independent and remain valid. Their proof
was independently audited in
`historical context (not an accepted premise)`.
The strict common support bound preserves saturated traces as actual sets.
The measure is exactly the original finite sum of positive d-dimensional
fiber volumes; no ambient volume or dimension-lowering approximation enters.

The ordinary paired centroid-tail theorem is used with its already proved
full all-direction scope. Its external dependency is an ordinary
one-constraint localization theorem, explicitly documented in that source;
neither theorem invokes OC. The ordinary simplex equality-normal statement
uses the classical equality case of continuous Grunbaum, not a mixed-body
classification. Those dependencies are stated accurately.

At the even sampled baseline, pair every nonzero base with its negative.
The positive own fiber forces any equality continuous normal to be a
canonical simplex vertex direction. For a nonzero integer displacement
s<=r the exact pair volume is the sum of (dr+s)^d and (dr-s)^d divided
by d!, strictly above the zero-shift value by strict convexity. At s>=r
one cap is full, of volume V_d r^d>2Gamma_d V_d r^d. The latter strict
inequality holds for all d>=2. Hence the active trace menu is precisely
the d+1 canonical cylinders, modulo the invisible integer directions.
This is enough for the stated positive compact gap to all other normals.

## 2. Every competing source and source uniqueness

The full vertex-permutation group is linear, fixes zero, and preserves
volume in absolute determinant. Its point orbit averages to zero by
barycentric-coordinate symmetry. Convexity of depth superlevel sets
therefore makes every fiber centroid a fiber maximum.

For a nonzero base z0, differentiating the ACTUAL proper vertex-cap
polynomial gives exactly

    -c_d z0 sum_z (r0_z)^(d-1).

This is a nonzero gradient, and the tilt direction z0 strictly lowers
the mass. Finite initial proper margins guarantee an actual open cap
chamber for a small positive tilt. Thus each nonzero base has a genuine
strict gap; there are finitely many bases, so a common positive gap
persists under the uniform cap-mass estimate. Orbit averaging covers
every point, not only the competing centroids.

At base zero the canonical normals span and sum to zero, so a nonzero
point has a strictly positive evaluation in some normal. Moving that
cap to pass through the point loses a positive own-fiber slab and gains
no other mass. The same argument applies to the optimized tilted caps.
Thus the global source is uniquely (0,0), as claimed.

## 3. Exact angular elimination and attained integer minimum

The retained simplex vertex height is (d-sum theta)r_z+alpha.z.
Its d edge drops are (d+1)r_z and the d-1 values
(d+1)(1-theta_j)r_z. Multiplying actual edge fractions proves (12)
with denominator d! times product(1-theta_j).

After s=1-sum(theta)/d and beta=alpha/s, the angular factor is
s^d/product(1-theta_j). The d positive numbers 1 and 1-theta_j
have arithmetic mean s. AM-GM gives factor >=1, with equality only
at theta=0. This is an exact factorization on the common proper
chamber, not a frozen-normal approximation.

The polynomial F_r has Hessian
d(d-1)/d! times sum(dr_z+beta.z)^(d-2)zz^T. Every coefficient
is positive, so it is positive definite on L. Its baseline gradient
is zero by evenness. The implicit-function theorem gives the unique
small critical beta, and strict convexity on a common convex proper
neighborhood makes it the unique local minimum. The angular Hessian
I-11^T/d has positive eigenvalues 1/d and 1; its multiplier is Q0.
The mixed angular/integer block is zero in the factored coordinates.

The full global compact gap is inherited uniformly from the baseline
complete menu. The same symmetric-difference estimate preserves it
under array perturbations; inside the charts exact factorization and
strict convexity identify the unique branch. Thus tau really is the
all-normal depth and the displayed caps are the complete active traces.
No local stationary calculation is substituted for this global step.

## 4. Full permutation orbits for slack sources

A cyclic vertex orbit would not necessarily span in general dimension;
the source correctly uses the FULL permutation group. The vertex-height
array of a nonzero normal lies in the d-dimensional zero-sum subspace.
Exchanging two unequal heights and subtracting their arrays gives a
nonzero coordinate difference. Permuting its indices generates all
coordinate differences, which span that subspace. Thus the full dual
normal orbit spans R^d and averages to zero. Equal positive orbit
weights give a covering family at the actual source base.

Every member is an actual attaining cap of the same strictly slack
mass. The family may have more than d+1 members and is not asserted
minimal. Assigning only its own base is sufficient. Frozen baseline
families retain coverage and slack, but are not falsely asserted to
remain critical; current criticality can instead be obtained by
reselection without a smooth-selection claim. The sign alpha.z0>0
follows because a cap cheaper than the deepest source cannot contain it.

## 5. Exact zero gain and all Hessian factors

F_r(0)=c_d sum r_z^d is a feasible canonical cap value. Strict convexity
and the all-normal result give tau=F_r(0) exactly when beta=0, equivalently
sum r_z^(d-1)z=0. The common continuous scaling gives exact global depth
Q0, preserves the actual lattice fibers and incidence, and proves the
nonnegative normalized mass gain with that precise nonlinear equality
condition.

At the even baseline the three derivatives are, with m=sum w_z v_z z,

    K=c_d(d-1)G_w/d,
    mixed=c_d(d-1)m,
    frozen=c_d d(d-1)sum w_z v_z^2.

Square completion gives the stated optimized second derivative and
beta'=-d G_w^dagger m. In differentiating M Q0/tau, the first-order
ratio terms cancel because M'=tau'/Gamma_d and M0=Q0/Gamma_d.
The normalized Hessian is therefore exactly
V_d d(d-1)m^T G_w^dagger m. It has rank k because v_z=a.z maps
onto G_w a in L. Compatibility of arbitrary sampled velocities is
not asserted. Since the normalized first derivative vanishes in
all sampled directions, acceleration terms indeed disappear along
actual C2 compatible paths.

## 6. Actual affine escape and boundary cases

Adding a.z on the ENTIRE fixed projection preserves concavity and,
for small a, uniform positivity. The candidate beta=-da cancels
every affine radius term inside the cap polynomial, leaving dr0_z.
Evenness makes its gradient zero, so unique local minimization and
the global gap give EXACT depth Q0. Pairwise strict convexity of
t^d yields strict mass increase for every nonzero a in L. The
first-volume derivative cancels within each parity class since z
and -z have the same parity and equal baseline weights.

P={0}, including n=0, has rank zero, absent integer tilt, ordinary
simplex depth, and no artificial positive escape. Rank-deficient
bases use the restricted inverse and invisible directions correctly.
d=1 is explicitly excluded because the strict integer curvature
and strict affine mass gain disappear there. Every assertion stays
in an above-OC local radial class for positive integer dimension.

## 7. Exact distinction between the tangent kernel and nonlinear zero gain

There is a useful ACTUAL d=3 calibration supporting the source's scope.
Take bases -2,-1,0,1,2 with even radii

    r0=(1/2,1,5/4,1,1/2),   v=(0,2,1,0,2).

The three discrete second differences of r0 are -1/4,-1/2,-1/4,
so piecewise-affine interpolation remains positive and concave for
both signs of sufficiently small radius perturbations r(t)=r0+t v.
The weighted tangent moment sum r0_z v_z z is zero, yet

    sum_z r_z(t)^2 z=4t^2.

Thus the compatible line is Hessian-null at zero but has strictly
positive normalized mass gain at every sufficiently small nonzero t
by the exact zero-gain theorem. It is not an all-order neutral line.
This example does not contradict any claim in the source; it confirms
why the nonlinear surface cannot be replaced by its tangent kernel.

Independent checker: `supporting computation verify_all_dimensional_radial_audit_slab_recovery.py`.

## 8. Added affine invariance and global l_d minimization

The subsequent Section 8 extension also passes. The exact identity
F_(r+a.z)(beta)=F_r(beta+da) gives the stated change in minimizing
coefficient and invariant tau wherever both actual arrays lie in the
validated neighborhood. The neighborhood can be shrunk uniformly so
all shifted small candidates remain in its original proper chambers;
alternatively the global norm representation below proves the same
invariance directly by translation of its unrestricted a variable.

The functional sum|r_z+a.z|^d is strictly convex for d>1 because the
linear evaluation map is injective on L. Its coercivity follows from
the triangle inequality and norm equivalence for this fixed injective
finite-dimensional map. The bounds are uniform for bounded nearby r.
Every sequence of minimizers for r tending to r0 is consequently
bounded; joint continuity makes each subsequential limit a minimizer
at r0, whose unique value of a is zero by symmetry and strict convexity.
This proves minimizer continuity at the baseline rather than assuming
it. The finite list of residuals is then strictly positive and the
minimizer belongs to the previous proper local neighborhood. Its
gradient equation agrees with (1) under beta=da, proving the exact
l_d-distance formula with the essential absolute values retained.
There is no constant term in the fitted subspace.

For any nearby actual r and nonzero small a, both signs preserve
continuous concavity and positivity on the whole compact projection.
Strict convexity gives M(r+a.z)+M(r-a.z)>2M(r), so at least one sign
has strictly more mass at exactly the same GLOBAL raw depth. Auxiliary
slack persists by the already proved finite source gaps. This rules
out a local fixed-depth mass maximum WITHIN the validated class when
k>0; it is not a general OC variational statement.
